objective: Proof with machine check: in the proved class with every knot live and at most five places, a ring-core start is a ring of L knots (L = 5 or L >= 7) with hung knots at least three apart, spare places only where the cap allows; its per-round count is the coefficient of a rational generating function with denominator 1 - W(z), W = z^n (1+z)^A prod (1 + z(1+z)^b); constant iff bare, else exponential at the root of W(1/x) = 1.
status: Proved 2026-11-19 (6 of 6 machine checks; referee pending): in the proved class with every knot live and at most five places, a start grows exponentially exactly when its core is a ring carrying a hung knot or a spare; per piece the count is [z^(t+1)] of a rational function with denominator 1 - W, W = z^n (1+z)^A prod (1 + z(1+z)^b); rate the root of W(1/x) = 1, at most the golden ratio; 23,098 rings of 5 to 14 knots grow exactly as the formula says.
title: Rings within five places: the eddies and their rates
